notes: Four subordinating and negative morphemes (מִן, בְּלִי, אֲשֶׁר, לֹא) stand against two English expressions ('so that', 'cannot'). 'so that' goes whole to the privative מִן on rule 48's own example, 'cannot' to the לֹא that negates the verb it stands on under rule 35, and בְּלִי and אֲשֶׁר are the unrendered occurrences under rule 22. The competing reading — rule 48's בְּלִי clause taking the negation and leaving לֹא unrepresented — is named in the unit note.
t017 'yet' is added: no conjunction morpheme stands in that clause, and rule 14's closing sentences forbid folding such a connective into the privative or the verb beside it.
s033-s034: the waw takes the bare 'even' and עַד the relational 'to', which is rule 16's count of two English words against two morphemes standing in the range phrase.
